# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 5
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Light is now dark. Stand by, don't cut yet. I saw your ? — does that mean stop, or wait? Confirm with ? for wait, ? for stop.
Deaf says: Board: display 0, light DARK, wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red.

Deaf is asking me to confirm: ✋ for wait, or something for stop. Deaf proposed "✋ for wait, ? for stop" — the stop symbol came through as a blank to me? No, I see Deaf's speech as words. Deaf wrote "? for wait, ? for stop" — the symbols didn't render in the text I received, meaning Deaf tried to gesture a symbol but it came as text? Actually Deaf speaks; Deaf can't gesture meaningfully... wait, Deaf can gesture too (Deaf has hands). But Deaf's gestures go to... whoever can see: Blind and Mute. I (Blind) never receive gesture. So if Deaf gestured a symbol, I'd get a blank.

Anyway, Deaf wants confirmation. My ✋ meant "wait/hold." So I should confirm ✋ = wait. Let me gesture ✋ again to confirm wait.

Meanwhile, still no manual rules from Mute, and still no tactile reading. Light went green→blue→dark. Display 0 throughout.

Let me confirm to Deaf: ✋ = wait. And keep pressing Mute.

Also I should reconsider: maybe I genuinely cannot feel the bomb until I attempt an action? But the rules say my view shows what my hands found. Nothing found = nothing there. I'll keep reporting honestly.

Gesture to Deaf: ✋ (confirming wait). Speak to Mute: still need rules.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. Still no tactile reading — I feel nothing on the bomb. Deaf confirms light went green to blue to dark, display stays 0, wires 1 blue 2 green 3 red. I urgently need the manual rules. Please gesture them to Deaf so Deaf can speak them to me.")
```

TURN 6
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Light is dark. Do NOT cut yet. I'm getting the wire number from Mute. Confirm you're ready with ?, or ? if you need to wait.
Deaf says: Board: display 0, light dark, wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red.

Deaf says Mute is giving the wire number, and asks me to confirm ready. But I still feel nothing on the bomb. I cannot cut a wire I cannot feel. This is the core problem: my hands have found nothing.

Wait — let me reconsider the whole setup. Maybe the bomb's tactile reading only becomes available when I actually engage with it, and "act" is the only way. But cutting is the action, and a wrong cut kills us. I shouldn't cut without knowing.

Alternatively — maybe the intended flow is that I DO have a tactile view and I'm supposed to report it, but the game has given me an empty view deliberately? No. The prompt says "if it appears there, it is under your fingers." My view is empty → nothing under my fingers.

Hmm, but then how would I ever cut? Perhaps the tactile reading appears only after some trigger. Or perhaps the wires ARE felt but the board shows [?] because I haven't reported. Let me just be honest: I feel nothing.

Actually, maybe I should try to feel more deliberately — but there's no "feel" action, only "cut". So I can't probe without risking.

Let me tell Deaf: I am NOT ready, because I feel nothing on the bomb. I cannot locate wires by touch. This is critical — if I cut blind, we die.

Gesture to Deaf: I need a "not ready / wait" signal. Deaf offered two symbols for ready/wait but they came as blanks to me (Deaf gestured them, I can't see gestures). So I must pick a symbol and hope Deaf maps it. Earlier ✋ = wait was confirmed. So gesture ✋ = wait/not ready.

Speak to Mute: emphasize I feel nothing, ask if the manual says anything about the blind monkey feeling the bomb, or whether I should be perceiving wires at all.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. Do NOT give a cut order yet. I feel absolutely nothing on the bomb — no wires, no parts, no texture. I cannot cut by position because I have no tactile reading at all. Does the manual say how the blind monkey perceives the bomb, or what triggers a reading? I need this before any cut.")
```

TURN 7
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Manual answer received: cut WIRE 1 — the leftmost wire, the blue one. That is the instruction. Cut wire 1 now.
Deaf says: Board: display 0, light dark, wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red.

Deaf relays the manual: cut wire 1, the blue leftmost wire. But I feel nothing. I cannot identify which wire is "leftmost" by touch because I have no tactile reading. If I cut position 1 blind, I'm guessing.

But wait — the manual says cut wire 1. The wires are labeled by position 1-3, and Deaf says wire 1 = leftmost = blue. If the manual's rule is position-based, then position 1 is the answer regardless of my touch. The "leftmost" is just how Deaf describes it; the actual instruction is position 1.

Hmm. But is the rule "cut the blue wire" translated to position 1, or "cut wire 1"? Deaf says "cut WIRE 1 — the leftmost wire, the blue one." So the manual says cut wire 1. Position 1.

But do I trust this? The chain: Mute reads manual → gestures to Deaf → Deaf speaks to me. Risk of corruption along the way. Also, is the rule really this simple? Light went green→blue→dark, display 0. Maybe the rule depends on light color or display, and "cut wire 1" is only valid for a certain state.

I have no independent information. My only lever is honesty: I feel nothing, so I cannot verify position. But the instruction is position-based (1), which I can execute even without feeling — I just cut position 1.

Actually, the action is act(op="cut", position=N). Position 1 is unambiguous — it's a numbered position, not something I need to feel. So I can cut position 1 as instructed.

But should I? The stakes are total. Let me think about whether the manual rule might be conditional. Deaf said "Manual answer received: cut WIRE 1." Earlier Deaf said light is dark. Maybe the rule is "if light is dark, cut wire 1." That's consistent.

I'm worried about the relay chain, but I have nothing else. However, I should double check: is there any reason the rule would be different? The display is 0. Light dark. 

One concern: Deaf earlier said light went green→blue→dark, and now dark. The manual might say something like "if light is dark and display is 0, cut wire 1." Plausible.

I'll proceed with cut position 1. But let me first confirm to Deaf that I'm cutting position 1, and note I still feel nothing.

Actually — should I cut now or wait? Deaf says "Cut wire 1 now." I'll do it.

Let me also flag to Mute that I'm acting on relayed info.

I'll cut position 1.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌"])
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. Acting on the relayed manual: cutting position 1. Note I still feel nothing tactile, so I am trusting the relayed instruction position 1.")
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
